newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds rose across the board in thin trading on Wednesday led by a rise in unlinked and dollar-linked bonds, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.12 pct to 100.92
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.11 pct to 100.79
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.13 pct to 101.34
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.23 pct to 101.16
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 pct to 100.80
Volume was a low 139 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds.
"Bonds are not interesting anymore. Investors are focusing on the stock market, which is more attractive now," said Yosi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.

"Most of the activity was concentrated in unlinked bonds, which are expected to become more attractive if the central bank decides to raise the reserve requirement," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.

Financial sources said on Tuesday that the Bank of Israel might raise the reserve requirement by five percentage points for commercial banks in an effort to combat growing liquidity in the economy. That would raise the requirement to between eight and 11 percent, depending on the term of the deposit.
"The banks will have to lower interests on short-term deposits and investors will then prefer to invest in Makams and unlinked bonds," Glicksberg said.
"Following the rise of the Makam, yields fell below 14 percent (for one year), which is regarded as very low," said one trader. "Yields on unlinked bonds also fell to 15 percent."
Glicksberg said inflation-linked long bonds had been rising on expectations of declining interest rates.
"After the release of December CPI it is clear that the Bank of Israel will not lower its base rate at the end of January. But in the long run the market expects such a reduction," he said.
The Central Bureau of Statistics announced after trading today that the consumer price index rose 0.8 percent in December, which was at the high end of expectations.
Dollar-linked bonds were today's main gainers. Traders said investors were responding to the rise of the dollar in world markets.
In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed on Wednesday at 3.2680 shekels against 3.2590 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.27 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
